result.text: A university enrollment system involves the following steps: Prospective students submit an application online.
The admissions office reviews the application and supporting documents.
If documents are missing, the applicant is notified to provide the missing items.
Upon receiving all documents, the application is evaluated by the admissions committee.
Concurrently, the finance department processes any application fees or waivers.
If the application is accepted, an acceptance letter is sent.
Otherwise, a rejection letter is sent and the process ends.
After being accepted, the student must then confirm enrollment by a specified deadline; otherwise the application will be canceled.
If the student confirms, they receive orientation materials and the IT department sets up student accounts for email, online portals, and library access.
If the student is international, the international student office assists with visa processing.
The student obtains a student ID card and starts creating their study plan, which includes: Meeting with an academic advisor.
Selecting courses.
Resolving any schedule conflicts.
The student begins attending classes.
Throughout each semester, the student may add or drop courses within the add/drop period.
At the end of the semester, grades are posted, and the student can review them online.
If the student has any grievances, they can file an appeal, which includes: Submitting an appeal form.
Meeting with the appeals committee.
Awaiting a decision.
The process repeats each semester until the student graduates or withdraws.

result.rule: When the description says a repeated cycle continues until the participant reaches one of several stated end outcomes, for example one outcome that ends the cycle by completing and another that ends it by leaving: Place a decision gateway at the end of the repeated cycle. Give it a loop-back branch to the start of the cycle for the continuing case, and a separate outgoing branch for each stated exit outcome. Model each exit outcome as its own activity on its branch, and do not let the exit branches merge back into the cycle.

When the description's final sentence says the process ends when one action is completed and a further named action is also carried out, the two joined by 'and' (for example, 'the X is done and the Y is executed'): Model each named closing action as its own task, in sequence, so that the later action is a task placed before the end event and the end event follows the last action. Do not drop the later action or fold it into the earlier task, and do not end the process at the first action.

When the description states that one activity is followed by two or more separate actions that all must happen, with no order stated between them, and the process continues only after all of them are done: Model a parallel gateway that splits the flow after the preceding activity into one branch per action, with each action as its own task. Close the branches with a parallel gateway before the next activity that needs all of them. Also place a parallel gateway around any activity the description lists as a separate, unordered step within such a group, so that each stated step keeps its own position in the flow. Do not use an exclusive gateway for branches that must all complete.

When the description states that a process ends once a final outcome is reached, while a later event such as customer feedback or a return may start additional steps that the main flow does not require: Model the final outcome as an explicit task placed before the end event. After the activity that leads to that outcome, place an exclusive gateway with one branch to the outcome and end event and a second branch to the optional follow-up path. Start the follow-up path from an intermediate catch event for the later trigger, or from a separate process or event subprocess, and join it back into the main flow only where the description says the process can continue. Do not drop the outcome step, the decision gateway, or the optional follow-up branch.
